extracted.intended_audience: PR professionals (agency and in-house), marketing managers, and anyone creating PR reports for stakeholders
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for creating PR reports and dashboards that communicate campaign impact to different audiences (executives, clients, internal teams), including recommended metrics, structure, format, cadence, and templates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exec-friendly one-pager
rubrics_metrics.description: A one-page summary that presents high-level results, perfect for senior stakeholders who need quick insights without getting bogged down in details.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present key metrics (like site traffic and sales generated) through a clear narrative arc: the challenge, the idea, the results. Focus on performance highlights and clear ROI. Keep it concise so executives can digest it quickly.

rubrics_metrics.name: PR supplement (concise snapshot for broader reports)
rubrics_metrics.description: A quick snapshot of digital coverage attached to a broader marketing or SEO report, showing campaign success in terms of links and authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this format for clients who don’t need full PR play-by-plays. Keep it top-level—show links, authority metrics and the handful of stats that matter. Supplement broader reports rather than duplicating full reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monthly deep-dive report
rubrics_metrics.description: A more detailed monthly report that starts with an exec summary and next steps, then provides deeper analysis of campaign activities, organic visibility, media coverage, and competitor analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report holistically across multiple channels and throughout the sales funnel. Put the executive summary and recommended next steps up front, followed by evidence: channel results, visibility metrics, coverage examples, and competitor context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Campaign wrap-up structure
rubrics_metrics.description: A structured campaign wrap-up that moves through Campaign Overview > Results > Wider Impact > Next Steps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow a logical, easy-to-read flow. Provide high-level performance summaries paired with sufficient context to explain impact. Use visual design tools (eg. Canva) to make the report visually pleasing and guide the reader’s eye.

rubrics_metrics.name: Live coverage dashboard (real-time reporting)
rubrics_metrics.description: A live dashboard that integrates cross-channel PR metrics (coverage authority, social shares, etc.) to monitor activity in real time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Best for internal teams or engaged clients who want minimal hand-holding and the ability to tweak campaigns on the fly. Note dashboards often give little context, so they suit users who can interpret raw metrics or who get regular walkthroughs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Answer a single specific question
rubrics_metrics.description: Focus your report on one clear goal or central question (a hypothesis) so you don't overwhelm the reader with information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of single questions: 'Did we drive traffic back to our site?', 'How much additional awareness did we create with influencers?', 'Did awareness convert into product sales?' A single-minded objective keeps reporting focused and actionable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep your audience front of mind
rubrics_metrics.description: Tailor report content, metrics, format, and cadence to what the audience actually cares about and how they prefer to consume information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ask: Do they really need this? What do they care about? How do they want it delivered? Senior execs typically want top-level impact and headlines; clients expect white-labeled context on deliverables; on-the-ground PRs need live, granular data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choose the right PR KPIs and metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Select KPIs that map to the audience and campaign goal (different audiences care about different measures).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: on-the-ground teams may track granular KPIs like number of dofollow links; C-suite wants top-level impact like share of voice uplift or site-level SOV vs competitors. Pick metrics that demonstrate alignment to business objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pick a format that fits (visuals, tools, and design)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use charts, graphs, and visuals to tell the story; pick tools that match your design and flexibility needs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Google Sheets/Docs are fine for manual reporting but limited for design; Looker Studio or Canva are recommended for more visual and flexible reports. Senior execs prefer well-designed top-level summaries; clients usually expect white-labeled reports; internal PRs need live dashboards or spreadsheets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Set the right reporting cadence
rubrics_metrics.description: Choose how often you report based on campaign goals and the audience—live, monthly, quarterly, yearly, or sales-cycle dependent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Internal teams: live/ongoing reporting. Senior execs/clients: monthly, quarterly, yearly, or aligned with sales cycles. Let the audience and the lag between activity and measurable outcomes determine cadence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow a simple narrative structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a loose formula to keep reports focused and valuable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommended structure: Exec summary (goal and campaign overview); Top wins; Expectation vs reality (curated charts that guide the story); Recommendations and next steps. Avoid over-reporting—curate charts to tell the narrative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use templates but customize per client
rubrics_metrics.description: Have reusable report templates to speed reporting, but delete irrelevant components and customize to the client’s needs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If unsure, ask the client how they want to see data. Custom templates take time but can be repurposed across clients and form a report library that improves efficiency and client satisfaction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary and Secondary KPIs for digital PR (Alex Jones framework)
rubrics_metrics.description: A set of primary 'owned' goals and secondary shared goals to include in digital PR reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Primary Owned Goals: volume of links; quality of links; relevance of links; domain rating; trust flow. Secondary Shared Goals (SSGs): keywords/rankings; traffic/sessions; conversions; revenue growth. Optionally add share of voice and sentiment if they contribute to client goals. Tie ranking/keyword changes to links acquired and impact on traffic/conversions/revenue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid over-reporting; stick to key insights and recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: Less is often more—prioritize clarity and actionability over exhaustive metrics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on a few curated insights and clear next steps. Too much data dilutes the message and reduces the likelihood stakeholders will act on recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include next steps early for time-pressed stakeholders
rubrics_metrics.description: Put recommended next steps and the most crucial info up front on page one for executives or time-pressed readers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ensures stakeholders immediately see what you recommend and why, without needing to dig through detailed charts or appendices.
